transcript.text: bosch 24 not draining, water sitting in bottom. help

If you mean Bosch error E24, it indicates a drainage problem. Water sitting in the bottom is consistent with that.

Try these steps in order:

1. Cancel/drain the cycle
• Open the door.
• On many Bosch models, press and hold Start for about 3 seconds until it says “Reset” or the drain pump starts.
• Close the door and let it attempt to drain for 1–2 minutes.

2. Clean the filter
• Turn off power to the dishwasher at the breaker if you’ll be reaching inside.
• Remove the bottom rack.
• Twist out the cylindrical filter assembly in the bottom center.
• Rinse it thoroughly and remove food debris/slime from the filter screen and sump area.

3. Check the drain pump area
• Scoop out standing water with a cup/towels first.
• Under/near the filter is a small pump cover. On many Bosch units it can be released carefully.
• Check for glass, labels, toothpicks, bones, etc. blocking the impeller.
• The impeller should move with slight resistance—not be jammed.

4. Check the sink/disposal connection
• Run the garbage disposal, if you have one.
• Check that the kitchen sink drains normally.
• If the dishwasher was recently installed or a new disposal was fitted, make sure the dishwasher inlet knockout plug on the disposal was removed. A forgotten plug causes immediate drainage failure.

5. Inspect the drain hose
• Under the sink, make sure the hose is not kinked, crushed, or clogged.
• It should be routed high up under the counter (“high loop”) or connected through an air gap, not lying low on the cabinet floor.

6. Try one more reset/drain
• Restore power, hold Start ~3 seconds, close the door, and listen:
• Pump hums but no water leaves: blockage in pump/hose/disposal connection is likely.
• No pump sound at all: possible failed drain pump, wiring, or control issue.

Avoid using chemical drain cleaner in the dishwasher—it can damage seals and create a hazard when you open it.

Call appliance service if the filter/pump area and hose are clear but it still won’t drain, especially if you hear a humming pump or repeatedly get E24. A Bosch technician may need to replace the drain pump or clear an internal blockage.
cleaned the filter, it was full of food gunk and a bit of broken glass. drains fine now, E:24 gone

Great — that was likely the whole issue. The clogged filter/glass was restricting the drain flow and triggering E:24.

A couple of quick precautions:

• Check the pump/impeller area once more for tiny glass pieces if you can safely access it.
• Run a short rinse cycle and confirm it fully drains again.
• Clean/rinse the filter every few weeks (more often if dishes go in with lots of food debris).
• Avoid putting glass shards or heavy food particles into the dishwasher; scrape plates first.

If E:24 returns despite a clean filter, then inspect the drain hose/pump area, but it sounds resolved.
